title: osstat LLM model registry
description: Seed data for the runnability advisor (ADR-008 / ROADMAP.md M4): the quantization levels the calculator prices models at, and the models themselves. This is data, not code, so the registry can grow without a release. Every number here is meant to be a real, sourced fact — a contributor adding a model should cite where a figure came from in `sourceNote` rather than estimate one.

version.description: Bumped whenever the shape of this file changes, so a future loader can tell old data from new.

quantLevels.description: The quantization levels the calculator evaluates every model at. Bit widths are approximate — GGUF k-quants mix precisions across tensor types — and are a property of the quantization scheme, not of any one model, which is why they live here once rather than being repeated per model.

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. Q4_K_M. Matches the llama.cpp quantization name.

bitsPerWeight.description: Average bits per weight, used to derive a file size from a parameter count.

description.description: What this level trades off, for the explanation drawer.

id.description: Stable slug, used as a React key and in the fit matrix.

family.description: Model family, for grouping in the UI.

parametersBillion.description: Total parameter count in billions, as published by the model's own card or technical report. Leave the model out of the registry entirely rather than guess this number.

sourceNote.description: Where the numbers above came from — a model card, technical report or config.json — so a reviewer can check them without re-deriving anything.

hiddenSize.description: Model dimension (hidden_size), kept for documentation even though the calculator derives head_dim independently.

numKvHeads.description: Key/value head count (num_key_value_heads) — equal to numAttentionHeads on a model with no grouped-query attention.

headDim.description: Per-head dimension. The KV cache scales with this and numKvHeads, not with hiddenSize directly, which is why it is stored rather than derived.

maxContextLength.description: The model's native maximum context (max_position_embeddings), used to cap the context-length control in the UI.
